name: CAMS no-show risk model
target: no_show = 1 when the patient did not attend the appointment (Kaggle 'No-show' = Yes)

features.name: age
features.description: Age in completed years on the appointment date
features.how_computed: years; the app derives it from date_of_birth

features.name: is_female
features.description: Sex coded 1 for F, 0 for M

features.name: lead_days
features.description: Whole days from the booking date to the appointment date
features.how_computed: appointment date minus the date the booking was made

features.name: prev_appointments
features.description: Number of the patient's earlier appointments whose outcome was known at booking time
features.how_computed: appointments dated strictly before the booking date

features.name: prev_no_show_rate
features.description: Share of those earlier appointments that were no-shows; missing when there are none
features.how_computed: no-shows divided by prev_appointments; NaN with no history

feature_function: ml/src/features.py: deployable_features() and age_in_years(); training calls the same function

training_data.dataset: Kaggle 'Medical Appointment No Shows' (joniarroba/noshowappointments), Vitória, Brazil

model.tuned_by: patient-grouped 5-fold cross-validation on the training part, by average precision; family chosen in E3

calibration.note: E8 found no calibration needed for the all-features model, because the out-of-fold Brier scores were the same to four decimals; the same comparison on this model is recorded in cv_brier_check

comparison_with_research_model.note: paired bootstrap, deployable minus research, same resampled patients

bands.low: predicted risk below the Medium threshold
bands.medium: risk at or above Medium and below High
bands.high: risk at or above the High threshold

thresholds.chosen_on: out-of-fold predictions of the training part (patient-grouped CV); the holdout only reports the result
thresholds.reasoning: The targets are the plan's: High is the lowest cut-off at which at least 40% of flagged bookings were no-shows (about twice the 20.6% training base rate) and Medium the same for 30%, both measured on out-of-fold predictions of the training part, never on the holdout, so the holdout stays an honest test. A cut-off must flag at least 1% of bookings so a lucky handful of top scores cannot set it, and precision must stay at or above the target at every higher cut-off. On the holdout, High flags 10.0% of bookings, 37.1% of them no-shows, catching 20.0% of all no-shows; Medium flags 58.6%, 27.4% precise, catching 86.7%. Holdout precision sits below the training figure because the holdout's base rate is lower and it has more patient history (see limitations). The model's ranking is modest (holdout AUC 0.727), so High is a short list for a reminder call and Medium is a broad 'above average' band. The flag is advisory: staff see Low, Medium or High next to a booking, the slot rule never changes, and no patient is refused or moved because of it.

intended_use: An ADVISORY flag shown to doctors and admins next to a booking (Low, Medium or High) so staff can decide whether to send a reminder or prepare a standby. It never decides who gets a slot: the slot rule is enforced by the database and is never relaxed, no patient is refused, moved or deprioritised because of the flag, and booking works unchanged if this model is missing or fails.
limitations: Uses age and sex as inputs. The flag is advisory only and must never be a reason to refuse, move or deprioritise a booking.

Trained on one public clinic dataset from Vitória, Brazil (Kaggle, appointments 29 April to 8 June 2016). It has not been validated on any other clinic. E6 shows that models using these same kinds of features lose a lot of AUC when moved between two datasets.
Patient history only exists from 29 April 2016, so it is sparse: 23.5% of training bookings had any earlier appointment, against 45.9% of holdout bookings. The app's history will be a different mix.

Probabilities are calibrated to this dataset's base rate (no-show rate 20.6% in the training part, 18.5% in the holdout). A clinic with a different base rate needs recalibrating before the probabilities are read as risks.

The ranking is modest (see metrics.holdout.auc_roc), so even the High band catches only a small share of all no-shows (see thresholds). Treat it as a nudge for a reminder call, not a prediction about one person.
No-shows in the training data are missed appointments only: the data has no cancellations, so the app's cancelled bookings are not modelled and are excluded from history.
No SMS, health-flag or neighbourhood information is used, because the app cannot collect it in version 1; the research models (E3, E4) show these add only a little AUC.
Scored on one time-based holdout (the latest 20% of appointment dates); intervals reflect sampling of patients, not a change of clinic or season.
